summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old woman was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea following consumption of cheese pizza, in the setting of chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic insufficiency. She presented with dehydration and symptoms consistent with fat malabsorption, including greasy, pale stools. Initial management included IV fluids, anti-nausea medication, and a clear liquid diet. Her symptoms improved rapidly, with resolution of vomiting and diarrhea by the next morning. She advanced to a regular diet without complications. Stool studies ruled out infectious causes including C. difficile, Salmonella, and Giardia. Her chronic conditions, including yeast infection, myalgias, and hypertension, were managed supportively. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to avoid fatty foods, continue Creon with meals, and follow up with her primary doctor regarding persistent muscle aches.
